title: Unified European Registry for Inherited Metabolic Diseases
summary: U-IMD is the first European database for all individuals diagnosed with an inherited metabolic disorder. Due to the rarity of these diseases, there is a great need to learn more about them in order to better understand the needs of patients and to improve diagnostic procedures, therapies, long-term management, and care. Because these are rare diseases, the study is being conducted simultaneously in various clinics within the European Union and also in clinics in other countries that collaborate with the European Reference Network for Inherited Metabolic Disorders (MetabERN). As part of the study, data on the course of the disease, treatment, laboratory values, results of technical examinations, and the results of developmental tests are collected and entered into the registry in pseudonymized form. Medical confidentiality and data protection regulations are strictly observed. The study is purely observational, and participation or non-participation has no impact on the treatment of patients. The data are subject to regular evaluations within the research consortium and are published in medical journals in compliance with data protection regulations.
conditions: All inborn error of metabolism as listed by the Inborn Errors of Metabolism Knowledgebase (https://iembase.org/).

interventions.name:
Examination of the clinical course and relevant laboratory, therapeutic, instrumental, and neuropsychological parameters. The parameters collected are consistent with current standard follow-up examinations. No additional parameters required solely for the study are collected.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children and adults with confirmed diagnosis of any inherited metabolic disease.
Written informed consent given by the patient, the parents or the legal representatives.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals with rare and unrelated serious comorbidities: 
Down syndrome 
Intraventricular haemorrhage (°III-IV)
Extreme low birth weight (<1,500 grams)
Severe hyperbilirubinemia with Kernicterus
Embryofetal alcohol syndrome
Intake of teratogenic drugs during pregnancy
